title: Team roles, permissions & collaboration
content:
## Understanding project roles

Every Emergent project has a **single owner** and can have any number of admins, members and viewers. Each role grants a different level of access to the project's resources, configuration and billing.

<Note title="Personal projects">
If you create a project on your own, you are the owner by default. You can invite collaborators at any time from the project settings.
</Note>

## Role capabilities

The table below shows what each role can do:

| Capability | Owner | Admin | Member | Viewer |
|------------|-------|-------|--------|--------|
| **View & test the app** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| **Chat with the agent** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | – |
| **Approve & deploy changes** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | – |
| **Edit project settings** | ✓ | ✓ | – | – |
| **Invite or remove members** | ✓ | ✓ | – | – |
| **Manage the database** | ✓ | ✓ | – | – |
| **Configure custom domain** | ✓ | ✓ | – | – |
| **View & manage billing** | ✓ | – | – | – |
| **Transfer ownership** | ✓ | – | – | – |
| **Delete the project** | ✓ | – | – | – |

<Callout type="info" title="Viewers can test but not modify">
Viewers are ideal for stakeholders, clients or QA testers who need to see the live app and its history but should not make changes.
</Callout>

## Shared credit pool

All projects draw from a **shared credit pool** that belongs to the owner's account. Every collaborator—regardless of role—uses credits from that pool when they interact with the agent or deploy changes.

- The owner's [credit balance](/credit-expiry-recharging) funds all project activity.
- Team members do not need their own credits or subscriptions.
- Usage by any team member is attributed to the owner's account for billing purposes.

<Warning title="Monitor usage in multi-user projects">
Because all team members share the same credit pool, it's important to track usage if you have a large team or are working on multiple projects simultaneously.
</Warning>

## Inviting team members

<Steps>
<Step title="Open project settings">
Navigate to your project and click the **Settings** icon in the top navigation bar (or sidebar, depending on your view).
</Step>

<Step title="Go to the Team tab">
Select **Team** from the settings menu to see the current list of collaborators.
</Step>

<Step title="Send an invite">
Enter the email address of the person you want to invite, choose their role from the dropdown (**Admin**, **Member** or **Viewer**), then click **Invite**.

They will receive an email with a link to accept the invitation and join the project.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Tip title="Invite by email only">
Invitations are sent to email addresses. The recipient must have (or create) an Emergent account with that email to accept the invite.
</Tip>

## Changing a member's role

Owners and admins can update any team member's role at any time:

1. Open **Settings → Team**.
2. Locate the member in the list.
3. Click the role dropdown next to their name and select the new role.
4. The change takes effect immediately—no email confirmation required.

<Note>
You cannot change your own role if you are the owner. To step down, you must first transfer ownership to another team member.
</Note>

## Removing a team member

Owners and admins can remove any member (including other admins) from the project:

1. Open **Settings → Team**.
2. Click the **Remove** button next to the member's name.
3. Confirm the action in the dialog.

Removed members immediately lose access to the project, including the chat history, codebase and deployed app configuration. They can be re-invited later if needed.

<Warning title="Removing an admin">
Admins can remove other admins. If you have multiple admins, coordinate role changes carefully to avoid accidental lockouts.
</Warning>

## Transferring ownership

Only the current owner can transfer ownership to another team member. Ownership transfer is **irreversible** and immediately moves billing responsibility and full control to the new owner.

<Steps>
<Step title="Open Team settings">
Go to **Settings → Team** in your project.
</Step>

<Step title="Select the new owner">
Find the team member you want to promote and click **Transfer ownership** next to their name.
</Step>

<Step title="Confirm the transfer">
You will be prompted to confirm. Once confirmed:

- The selected member becomes the **Owner**.
- You become an **Admin** (or can be assigned a different role by the new owner).
- The new owner's account takes over billing and credit management for the project.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Danger title="Ownership transfer is permanent">
You cannot undo an ownership transfer. The new owner will have full control, including the ability to remove you from the project or delete it entirely.
</Danger>

## Best practices for team collaboration

- **Assign roles conservatively**: Grant the minimum permissions needed for each team member's responsibilities.
- **Use viewers for external stakeholders**: Clients, investors or non-technical collaborators can see progress without risking accidental changes.
- **Communicate before transferring ownership**: Ensure the new owner understands they will inherit billing and full administrative control.
- **Monitor the credit pool**: Keep an eye on usage if your team is large or actively iterating—credits are shared across all collaborators.

For more on how credits work and recharge policies, see [Credit expiry & recharging](/credit-expiry-recharging).
description: Four project roles (Owner/Admin/Member/Viewer) with a capability matrix, a shared credit pool, inviting members, changing roles, and transferring ownership.
